title: Damphu indoor weekly religious gatherings and utility dispute
reason: Not a qualifying protest: the specific 13 October indoor religious gathering is reported at around 30 people; a separate 40–50 range is not assigned to that date. The article describes a private religious meeting and an owner’s individual letter, not a public protest or participants’ collective demand.
notes: Subsequent November/December reporting concerns the same private gatherings and court dispute; it is not treated as a protest continuation.

title: Bhutan Innovation Forum, Paro
reason: A policy/innovation forum, not a protest. A September opinion author urged Forum speakers to raise issues, but no attendee adoption/action is reported. BBS’s 1,000+ figure is prospective attendance; post-event reporting gives no actual total.
notes: Forum held 1–3 October at Dungkar Dzong, Paro. No evidence of a participant collective demand against the government.

title: 16 Days of Activism campaign-design workshop
reason: The UN report states 55 people attended a three-day workshop to design media campaigns. It was a workshop, not an executed public protest, and does not report a collective demand directed at Bhutanese authorities.
notes: The UN report was published 20 October, but it does not date the three-day workshop; publication date is not used as event date. No executed launch action was established.
